newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG mercenary report on hold till after election.
newsitem.headline: PNG mercenary report on hold till after election.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea government said on Thursday the findings of an inquiry into a failed plan to hire mercenaries to put down an island uprising were unlikely to be revealed until after an election next month.

Acting prime minister John Giheno on Thursday received the 125-report from Judge Warwick Andrew's inquiry into the US$36 million deal with African mercenaries to put down the nine-year secessionist rebellion on Bougainville island.
But Giheno told reporters he expected it would take him between two and three weeks to read the report before he could decide when, or if, to release it publicly.
"I need time to actually look at the recommendations before I can release it to the public," Giheno said.
"If I feel that it is in the interest of the public that I should be releasing the report, then I will do so."
A scheduled election in the South Pacific nation will begin on June 14 and is expected to take three weeks to complete.

Giheno was appointed after Sir Julius Chan agreed to step aside last March pending an inquiry into the decision to hire London-based military consultancy Sandline International to end the Bougainville rebellion and re-open a vast copper mine.
The mercenary contract was opposed by former military chief Brigadier General Jerry Singirok, who was sacked by Chan, sparking an army revolt and the nation's worst crisis since independence in 1975.
